clue.text: Enclosure surrounded by iron border

indicators.note: the enclosure word sits within the iron symbol, which wraps round it on both sides

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a ring is an enclosed area, as in a boxing or circus ring

explanation.surface: A paddock or pen ringed by an iron fence along its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe is the outer edge or margin of something, a synonym of border.

clue.text: A medley of jazz music in Portuguese resort

indicators.note: the jazz word is placed within the name of the resort town

parts.note: Faro is a resort town on Portugal's Algarve coast
rag, short for ragtime, is an early style of jazz

explanation.surface: A mixed programme of jazz being played at a holiday spot in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture or hotchpotch, much like a medley.

clue.text: Put in a grave opinion during a TV investigation

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body in a grave
a view is a personal opinion

explanation.surface: Someone voices a serious opinion in the middle of a television investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' reads as the adjective 'serious', but it belongs with 'Put in a' as the burial sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A television interview questions a subject closely, a kind of on-screen investigation.

clue.text: Dark blue

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both dim, murky lighting and a downcast, melancholy mood.

clue.text: Two things a lodger may require with a computer

parts.words: Two things a lodger may require
parts.note: a lodger needs a door key and also board, meaning meals provided with the room

parts.words: Two things a lodger may require
parts.note: a lodger needs a door key and also board, meaning meals provided with the room

explanation.surface: A list of a lodger's needs, ending oddly with a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' here is the old sense of meals supplied with lodgings, as in 'bed and board'.
explanation.definitionFit: The typing device is the part used with a computer to enter text.

clue.text: English style school

parts.note: ton is fashionable style, from the French 'bon ton'

explanation.surface: A school run along traditional English lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English style school' reads as one description, but it splits into three jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English private school near Windsor.

clue.text: Plucky player shut out supporter

parts.note: to ban someone is to exclude or shut them out
a joist is a beam that supports a floor or ceiling

explanation.surface: A brave sportsman is excluded by a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucky' suggests courage, but the instrument player plucks strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is played by plucking its strings, so its musician is a plucking performer.

clue.text: A collection in a church service

definitions.note: noun in the clue for a verb answer: to gather things into a heap or collection

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic eucharistic service

explanation.surface: The offertory plate passed round during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the church collection; the definition is the gathering sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate is to build up a large collection or store of things.

clue.text: Dingy church has a place in modern history

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
kirk is the Scottish word for a church

explanation.surface: A drab old church that played its part in recent history.
explanation.definitionFit: The French port saw the 1940 evacuation of Allied troops, a famous event of modern times.

clue.text: Share it with Nora, perhaps

indicators.note: signals that the letters given might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Telling someone to split something with a friend called Nora.
explanation.definitionFit: An allocated share or allowance of food or supplies is a fixed portion.

clue.text: Man out in storm reaching peak

indicators.note: a storm throws things about, so the preceding words are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A climber caught in bad weather making it to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' rearranges MAN OUT into MOUNTA, with 'in' kept as written at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is a high summit, standing for the whole elevated landform.

clue.text: Chief required in some lawless state

indicators.note: the chief word is needed inside the word for 'some', so it goes within it

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'
arch means chief or principal, as in archenemy

explanation.surface: A country without laws needs a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition with no government or order is a state without law.

clue.text: Bitterness shown by army CO in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed and stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Resentment in the ranks when the commanding officer gets into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is fodder and 'trouble' alone signals the rearrangement. CO is commanding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is harsh, angry ill-feeling, a synonym for bitterness.

clue.text: Such trees may be different but there's no great variety

definitions.text: Such trees may be different but there's no great variety

parts.words: Such trees may be different but there's no great variety
parts.note: the miniature potted trees come in many species, yet none is great in size: 'great variety' puns on large kinds

explanation.surface: A remark that some trees vary but offer little choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no great variety' seems to mean little range, but means no large type: all these trees are dwarfed.
explanation.definitionFit: These Japanese-style trees are kept artificially tiny, so no kind among them is large.

clue.text: Love to take part in new survey of peeping Toms

indicators.note: the love letter joins in, entering among the other letters
makes the following word into a fresh arrangement of its letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic joins a fresh study of people who spy on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns SURVEY into VYEURS; 'to take part in' places O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeping Tom secretly watches others undressing, the same as a voyeur.

clue.text: God of love, not harmony

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a din is a loud discordant noise, the opposite of harmony

explanation.surface: A deity of love who brings no peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God of love' suggests Cupid or Eros, but 'love' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief deity of Norse mythology, ruler of Asgard.

clue.text: Sweepstake?

parts.note: read as 'sweep stake', a wooden pole for sweeping, rather than a betting pool

explanation.walkthrough: A sweepstake is a lottery on a race; the question mark invites reading it as a stake, or stick, used to sweep.
explanation.definitionFit: The long handle of a brush for sweeping floors is a wooden pole.

clue.text: Trial, I see, is translated in Hebrew

indicators.note: translating converts words into another form, so these letters change into a new order

explanation.surface: A court case rendered into the Hebrew language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hebrew' looks like the language, but here it names a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebrew in the biblical sense is a member of the ancient people of Israel.

clue.text: Spot of wet weather

parts.note: a 'spot of' weather sounds like a brief spell, but a spot is literally one drop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot of wet weather' sounds like a short shower; it is literally one spot of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A single falling bead of water from a shower is one spot of it.

clue.text: Loathed new fashion — looks slovenly

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A scruffy dresser hates the latest trends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new fashion' reads as the latest style, but 'new' is fodder and 'fashion' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes shoes worn down at the back, hence shabby and neglected in appearance.

clue.text: His work increases day by day

definitions.text: His work increases day by day

parts.words: His work increases day by day
parts.note: a journal keeper adds a new entry every day, so the writing grows daily

explanation.walkthrough: 'day by day' sounds like gradual growth, but means one daily entry after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps a daily journal writes in it each day.

clue.text: Cut the corn

definitions.meaning: to trim short, as with hair
the harvest or yield of a grain field

explanation.surface: An instruction to harvest the corn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to trim closely and the gathered produce of a field.

clue.text: He has a complaint, but [he] is prepared to wait

definitions.meaning: someone under medical care for an illness or ailment
adjective sense: tolerant of delay without fuss

explanation.surface: A grumbler who nonetheless stays calm about the delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' suggests grumbling, but it is a medical ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is someone receiving medical treatment; the adjective is calmly willing to bear delay.

clue.text: A dandy, too

parts.note: a swell is an old word for a fashionable, well-dressed man

explanation.surface: Someone else is also a fop.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means also or in addition, a synonym for too.

clue.text: Throw out an egg I found no longer fresh

indicators.note: throwing letters out of place jumbles them into a new order

explanation.surface: Discarding an egg that has gone stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw out' seems to mean discard the egg, but it signals rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing old means losing youthful freshness.

clue.text: Actor in a run

definitions.meaning: a minor film performer in a crowd scene, with no lines
in cricket, a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or bye

explanation.surface: A performer appearing in a long run of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a run' suggests a stage run; in cricket, an extra is a run not hit by the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a background film performer and a cricket run given away by the fielding side.

clue.text: A possible customer survey

definitions.meaning: a potential buyer or client being courted
verb sense: to look over or explore an area, as for gold

explanation.surface: A market survey of potential buyers.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a likely client; the verb means to search or examine ground.

clue.text: Go by a mountain road

definitions.meaning: a route through a gap between peaks

explanation.surface: Travelling along a road through the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to move past; the noun is a gap or col through high ground.

clue.text: A pause in travel abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A break taken during a trip overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' looks like part of the trip, but it signals rearranging TRAVEL into TERVAL, after IN as written.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a break or gap between events, such as one in a theatre.

clue.text: With passion returning during exam, see red

indicators.note: the passion word comes in the middle of the exam abbreviation

parts.note: CSE was the Certificate of Secondary Education, an old British school exam

indicators.note: the anger word comes back, read from its end to its start

parts.note: ire is anger, a fierce passion

explanation.surface: A furious outburst in the middle of a test, seeing red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see red' suggests rage; 'see' is a link and 'red' the definition. 'returning' makes ERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a bright cherry-coloured shade of red.

clue.text: He's not on speaking terms with his brothers

definitions.text: He's not on speaking terms with his brothers

parts.words: He's not on speaking terms with his brothers
parts.note: a monk of an order keeping strict silence does not talk with his fellow monks

explanation.walkthrough: 'not on speaking terms' suggests a family quarrel; the 'brothers' are monks under a vow of silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks of this Cistercian order are known for their rule of silence.

clue.text: A student has to live with it though

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car
to be means to exist or live

explanation.surface: A student must put up with it, however reluctantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means even though or although.
